body:
### What happens

Since the #234 changes to the release conditions, the **Release** job in `js.yml` (and **Rust CI/CD / Auto Release** in `rust.yml`) is `skipped` on every push to `main`, even when every job it `needs` succeeded. Nothing has been published since. For example, `feat(docker): support memory reservation across launch and resume` (a0e08168, #236) is merged, but npm `start-command` is still `0.38.0`.

The resource fix #239 (for #238) is also merged but unpublished. Downstream hosts therefore keep the 1 s cgroup sampler: measured on start-command 0.37.8 in link-assistant/hive-mind, it costs 0.25–0.30 cores per running task (36 rounds per minute each). #242 and #243 depend on the same release path.

| Run (push to main) | Head | `needs` results | Release |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [39283178442](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/actions/runs/39283178442) | 60a7de12 | syntax-check, lint, test ×3, coverage, parity: all `success` | `skipped` |
| [39503701792](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/actions/runs/39503701792) | 20e1d179 | all `success` | `skipped` |
| [39555219842](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/actions/runs/39555219842) | 3d11f6bf | all `success` (Rust: all needs `success` too) | `skipped` (Auto Release `skipped`) |

The last release that did run was at 7a89d034 (`rust-v0.27.0`). At that point the conditions compared named results:

```yaml
# rust.yml @ 7a89d034: released
needs: [lint, test, build]
if: |
  !cancelled() &&
  github.event_name == 'push' &&
  github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' &&
  needs.build.result == 'success'
```

Now both files use:

```yaml
# js.yml @ 3d11f6bf: always skipped
needs: [syntax-check, lint, test, coverage, parity]
if: |
  !cancelled() &&
  github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' &&
  github.event_name == 'push' &&
  !contains(needs.*.result, 'failure') &&
  !contains(needs.*.result, 'cancelled') &&
  !contains(needs.*.result, 'skipped')
```

The block-scalar form itself worked before, so the change in the result checks (and the longer `needs` list) is the prime suspect. I could not see from the run UI which term was false: a skipped job logs nothing about its `if`.

### Reproduce

Push any commit to `main` and look at the Release job in the JavaScript workflow run.

### Workaround

- Run the workflow with `workflow_dispatch` (`instant-release`) to publish what is on `main`.
- Downstream, link-assistant/hive-mind applies `docker update --memory-reservation` itself until a release with #236 is on npm (https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/pull/3531).

### Suggested fix

1. Compare each needed result explicitly, as the last working version did:

   ```yaml
   if: >-
     ${{ !cancelled() && github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' &&
         needs.syntax-check.result == 'success' && needs.lint.result == 'success' &&
         needs.test.result == 'success' && needs.coverage.result == 'success' &&
         needs.parity.result == 'success' }}
   ```

   Do the same for `auto-release` in `rust.yml`.
2. To confirm the root cause first, add a step that always runs (in `pipeline-status`, for example), and print `${{ toJSON(needs) }}` together with the value of each term of the condition, so the next skip shows which term was false.
3. Add a check to `pipeline-status` that fails on `main` push runs when Release is `skipped` while all of its needs succeeded, so a silent "nothing released" cannot happen again.
title: Release / Auto Release are skipped on every push to main since #234, although all needed jobs succeed (nothing published since 0.38.0)
